assets.credit: Solar System Scope / INOVE, based on NASA imagery
assets.projection: Equirectangular; north at image top; repeat horizontally, clamp at poles.
assets.preparation: 8192x4096 source downsampled to 4096x2048 with Lanczos, JPEG quality 94, no recoloring.
assets.limitations: NASA-derived processed surface map. Provider tunes colors and fills unmapped gaps; not calibrated scientific albedo.
assets.rendering_guidance: Neutral gray, cratered dry body. Hard terminator, virtually no atmospheric rim. Avoid globally embossed relief unrelated to light.

assets.credit: Solar System Scope / INOVE, based on NASA imagery
assets.projection: Equirectangular; north at image top; repeat horizontally, clamp at poles.
assets.preparation: Unmodified source copied as production filename.
assets.limitations: Visible-cloud visualization, not a surface radar map. Strong cloud markings and yellow are deliberately enhanced; do not label the raw texture natural color.
assets.rendering_guidance: Reduce contrast strongly and mix toward pale ivory/cream in shader; use only about 10-20% of source variation. Visible-light Venus is relatively featureless; strong UV cloud pattern is an optional clearly labeled enhanced view.

assets.credit: Solar System Scope / INOVE, based on NASA imagery
assets.projection: Equirectangular; north at image top; repeat horizontally, clamp at poles.
assets.preparation: 8192x4096 source downsampled to 4096x2048 with Lanczos, JPEG quality 94, no recoloring.
assets.limitations: NASA-derived processed surface map with provider color saturation, terrain compositing and possible gap filling. Polar coverage/atmospheric state is representative, not today.
assets.rendering_guidance: Rust/ochre geology, dark albedo regions, white ice. Source orange is saturated; reduce saturation modestly in renderer and retain thin understated dusty atmosphere.

assets.credit: Solar System Scope / INOVE, based on NASA imagery
assets.projection: Equirectangular; north at image top; repeat horizontally, clamp at poles.
assets.preparation: Native 2048x1024 source resampled to 4096x2048 with Lanczos for consistent texture dimensions. No added detail or recoloring.
assets.limitations: 4k is a resampled asset, not 4k observational detail. Broad smooth cyan haze represents atmospheric appearance. Provider enhances color and fills gaps.
assets.rendering_guidance: Pale cyan, subtle bands, restrained haze. Avoid adding dramatic cloud storms or glowing rings. Axial tilt is the meaningful visual distinction.

assets.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Björn Jónsson; Askaniy Anpilogov (2018); Karkoschka, E. (1994)
assets.projection: Equirectangular; north at image top; repeat horizontally, clamp at poles.
assets.preparation: Source 4096x2048 saved as JPEG quality 94; no color changes or invented details.
assets.limitations: Historic Voyager-based map, improved/recolored by Celestia contributor; dark storms are historical, not current weather. Colors approximate natural muted blue but not a newly calibrated 2024 spectrum-derived reconstruction.
assets.rendering_guidance: Already muted gray-blue/cyan, suitable without neon-blue tinting. Keep pale cloud features and diffuse atmosphere; do not paint a synthetic storm over the existing one.

color_references.finding: Oxford study of STIS/MUSE and rebalanced Voyager/WFC3 data reports Uranus and Neptune similar pale greenish-blue; Neptune only slightly bluer. Common vivid Neptune imagery was stretched/enhanced.
NASA documents slight true-color Uranus contrasts; extreme bands and orange/yellow limb in the false-color view are image processing artifacts.
NASA distinguishes comparatively featureless visible-light Venus from highly patterned ultraviolet views.
Galileo Venus cloud patterns use violet filter, high-pass filtering and colorization, not unaltered visible-eye color.
